Epidemiological studies have suggested that increased dietary fish intake is associated with a reduced risk of fatal coronary events,13 and possibly also ischaemic stroke,14,15 and there is also evidence for benefit with omega-3 fatty acid supplements, particularly for secondary preven- tion.1-4,16 In the GISSI-Prevenzione study,17 long-term use of omega-3 fatty acid supplements reduced the risk of fatal cardio- vascular events in a large group of Italian post-infarction patients studied for 3.5 years,17 while the JELIS investigators18 reported a reduction in primary and secondary cardiovascular events in Japanese patients with hypercholesterolaemia. However, a sys- tematic review19 found no clear benefit from omega-3 fatty acids, whether dietary or supplemental, in people with or without cardiac risk factors. 1. Carroll DN, Roth MT.
